name: Pettee Hall
use: College of Health and Human Services departments (Family Studies / Human Development, Social Work) and the NH Institute for Health Policy and Practice (as of 2001)
architect: Eric T. Huddleston; 1998–2001 renovation by JSA, Inc.
style: Colonial Revival (the renovated entrance has a cast-stone portico)

renovations.what: Extensive renovation (exterior work by JSA, Inc. from 1998); rededicated March 2, 2001

facts.text: Built for home economics, agricultural engineering and military science.
Named for Dean Charles H. Pettee, who served the college for 62 years and was three times interim president.

more.label: UNH Library Archives: academic buildings history

verdict: 1938 Colonial Revival hall for Health and Human Services, rebuilt in 2001 behind a crisp stone-trimmed portico.
notes: Old data's 1997 fire-code closure and ~$5M cost not verified. Current occupants beyond the archives' 2001 list unconfirmed. The 2005 Commons photo shows a crisp renovated brick front with a stone-trimmed portico. No interior evidence; no reviews.
judgeNotes: Photo of the renovated front; nothing documented about the interior.
